This is the Brazen Bull, and legend calls it the cruelest punishment ever made.
About two thousand six hundred years ago, a ruler named Phalaris ran a city on the island of Sicily.
The story says an artist from Athens built him a giant bull out of bronze, hollow inside, with a door in its side.
Prisoners were locked in, and a fire was lit underneath.
Pipes in its head were said to turn their cries into the sound of a bull.
But the ruler was so disgusted, he made the inventor test it first.
Years later, his own people rose up, and legend says Phalaris ended up inside his own bull.
But historians aren't sure any of it happened. The full story was written down about five hundred years later.
Many think it was made up to show how evil a ruler could be.
Here's the twist. A bronze bull really did exist. Soldiers from Carthage carried it off when they captured the city.
Centuries later, a Roman general captured Carthage and sent the bull back home.
A Roman writer said it was a reminder of how cruel their old rulers had been.
But one historian thinks it may have just been a statue honoring a river.
Today the bull is lost, so we may never know the truth.
